keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «돈이 더 많으면 더 행복할 것이라는 많은 사람의 믿음(흔한 생각)» 과 «돈은 특히 기본적인 필요를 채워 어느 정도의 행복을 살 수 있지만, 그것이 전부는 아니다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the common belief (if people just had more money, they would be happier) and the conclusion (money can buy a certain amount of happiness, especially by meeting basic needs, but it is not the whole story). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.qko: 돈은 언제 행복에 가장 큰 도움이 되나요?
boxes.qen: When does money help happiness most?
boxes.a: When basic needs are not met; the effect gets weaker as people grow richer
Experiences, giving to others, relationships, health, and purpose

qs.q: Why can extra income greatly improve the lives of very poor families?
qs.qko: 추가 소득은 왜 아주 가난한 가정의 삶을 크게 나아지게 할 수 있나요?
opts: Because they already have everything they need
Because they cannot pay for basics like food and housing, which causes constant stress
Because they spend all their money on trips with friends
evs: Yet a well-known study from 1978 found that lottery winners were not much happier than people who had not won.
A family that cannot pay for food, housing, or medical care faces constant stress.
Research suggests that spending on experiences, such as trips with friends, often brings more lasting joy than buying objects.
In addition, many factors that strongly affect happiness cannot be bought, including close relationships, good health, and a sense of purpose.
why: 음식, 집, 병원비를 낼 수 없는 가정은 늘 스트레스를 받아요. 그래서 이런 사람들에게는 추가 소득이 삶을 크게 나아지게 해요.
A family that cannot pay for food, housing, or medical care faces constant stress, so extra income helps them a lot.

qs.q: In the text, what does 'diminishing returns' mean?
qs.qko: 글에서 'diminishing returns(수확 체감)' 은 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: Each extra amount of money adds less happiness than before
People lose money as they become richer
Happiness always rises at the same speed as income
evs: However, the effect becomes weaker as people grow richer.
Interestingly, how people spend money may matter as much as how much they have.
Moving from very poor to comfortable makes a big difference, but moving from rich to very rich usually changes much less.
why: 부자가 될수록 돈의 효과가 약해지고, 아주 가난하다가 넉넉해지는 것은 큰 차이를 만들지만 부자에서 큰 부자가 되는 것은 차이가 훨씬 작다고 해요. 돈이 늘어날수록 더해지는 행복은 줄어든다는 뜻이에요.
The effect becomes weaker as people grow richer: going from very poor to comfortable matters a lot, but going from rich to very rich changes much less.

qs.q: What does the text suggest about how to spend money for more happiness?
qs.qko: 더 행복해지려면 돈을 어떻게 쓰라고 글은 말하나요?
opts: Save every coin and never spend it
Buy as many new objects as possible
Spend it on experiences and on other people
evs: Research suggests that spending on experiences, such as trips with friends, often brings more lasting joy than buying objects.
First, money clearly matters when people do not have enough of it.
Spending money on other people, for example by giving gifts or donating, can also increase happiness.
Economists often explain this with the idea of diminishing returns.
why: 친구와의 여행 같은 경험에 쓰면 오래가는 기쁨을 얻고, 선물이나 기부처럼 다른 사람을 위해 써도 행복이 커질 수 있어요. 두 문장을 합쳐야 해요.
Spending on experiences brings lasting joy, and spending on others can also increase happiness. You need both sentences.

ends: Why do experiences make us happier than things?
왜 물건보다 경험이 우리를 더 행복하게 할까?
How can giving to others make us happier?
다른 사람에게 베푸는 일은 어떻게 우리를 더 행복하게 할까?

write.howtoKo: 예문을 틀로 삼아, 빈칸 두 곳을 «중요한 일 + 그 이유» 로 바꿔 영어로 써 보세요.
write.howtoEn: Use the example as a pattern. Write an important action and your reason in English.
write.src: “It is important to <u>spend time with the people we love</u> because <u>close relationships cannot be bought</u>.”

write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «because» 뒤에 «무엇이 + 어떤지» 를 넣어 이유를 분명하게 써 보세요. (예: because good memories last a long time)
write.moreEn: One more step: after «because», write what + what it is like to make your reason clear. (e.g. because good memories last a long time)
